name: bepirovirsen
uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE HIBSAGO is indicated in combination with nucleos(t)ide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NrtI) therapy for treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adult patients without cirrhosis: • who have been on NrtI therapy for at least 6 months and have suppressed HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and • who have HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) levels less than or equal to 3,000 IU/mL as determined by an FDA-authorized test [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.2 )] . HIBSAGO is a hepatitis B virus (HBV) mRNA-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) indicated in combination with nucleos(t)ide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NrtI) therapy for treatment of chronic HBV infection in adult patients without cirrhosis: • who have been on NrtI therapy for at least 6 months and have suppressed HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and • who have HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) levels less than or equal to 3,000 IU/mL as determined by an FDA-authorized test. ( 2.2 )
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of HIBSAGO have not been established in patients less than 18 years of age.
boxed: WARNING: ON-TREATMENT HEPATIC FLARES AND THROMBOCYTOPENIA On-Treatment Hepatic Flares HIBSAGO may cause on-treatment hepatic flares with increases in ALT of >20-40x ULN associated with decline in HBsAg. Some cases were associated with hyperbilirubinemia. Most occurred in the first 12 weeks of treatment and resolved when treatment was interrupted or permanently discontinued [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ), Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 )] . ALT and total bilirubin must be measured prior to initiation of HIBSAGO and frequently monitored during treatment [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.4 ), Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] . Do not initiate HIBSAGO in patients with evidence of acute hepatic impairment or cirrhosis [see Contraindications ( 4 )] . Interruption of treatment, followed by reducing the dose or discontinuation of HIBSAGO, may be necessary based on the results of liver laboratory tests [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.4 )] . Thrombocytopenia HIBSAGO may cause reductions in platelet counts that may result in sudden and unpredictable thrombocytopenia, which can be life-threatening. Prior to starting HIBSAGO, obtain a platelet count to ensure the patient is eligible for treatment [see Contraindications ( 4 )] . HIBSAGO is contraindicated in patients with a platelet count below 100 x 10 9 /L prior to initiation of treatment. During treatment, monitor platelet counts weekly if values are 75 x 10 9 /L or greater, and more frequently if values are less than 75 x 10 9 /L  ...
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS HIBSAGO is contraindicated in patients: • with acute hepatic impairment, or cirrhosis who have mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A, B, or C) [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] . • with a platelet count below 100 x 10 9 /L prior to initiation of treatment [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )] . • Patients with acute hepatic impairment, or cirrhosis who have mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A, B or C) ( 4 , 5.1 ) • Patients with platelet count below 100 x 10 9 /L prior to initiation of treatment ( 4 , 5.2 )
interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS • Monitor patients for signs of bleeding and thrombocytopenia if HIBSAGO is taken concomitantly with anticoagulants, antiplatelets or drugs that decrease platelet count. ( 7.1 ) • Monitor patients for signs of worsening renal function during concomitant administration of HIBSAGO with drugs that may impair renal function. ( 7.2 ) • Concomitant administration of HIBSAGO and peginterferon alfa-2a is not recommended. ( 7.3 ) 7.1 Anticoagulants, Antiplatelets, and Drugs that Decrease Platelet Count Monitor patients for signs of bleeding and thrombocytopenia if HIBSAGO is taken concomitantly with anticoagulants, antiplatelets, or drugs that decrease platelet count [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 ), Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 )] . 7.2 Drugs that Impair Renal Function Monitor patients for signs of worsening renal function during concomitant administration of HIBSAGO with drugs that may impair renal function. Refer to individual drug information before prescribing [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 ), Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 )] . 7.3 Peginterferon Alfa-2a Concomitant administration of HIBSAGO and peginterferon alfa‑2a is not recommended due to the potential for an exacerbated risk of increased ALT, decreased platelet count, and immune-mediated effects.
